title: Court Marriage in Bangladesh 2026: Procedure, Documents, Notary Affidavit & Lawyer Fees
metaTitle: Court Marriage in Bangladesh 2026 | Rules, Cost & Documents
metaDescription: Complete legal guide on Court Marriage in Bangladesh. Learn about notary public affidavits, Nikahnama registration fees, required documents, and protection against false police cases.
heroIntro: In Bangladesh, what is colloquially known as "Court Marriage" is legally a combined two-step procedure: executing a Declaration of Marriage Affidavit before a 1st Class Magistrate or Notary Public and completing statutory Nikahnama registration under the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974. Authored by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Lawyer. For discreet and confidential legal assistance, call our Uttara chamber at 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Fast Facts: Court Marriage in Bangladesh (2026)
points: Statutory Age: Groom must be at least 21 years old and bride at least 18 years old.
Mandatory Documents: National ID Cards (NID) or digital online birth certificates, passport photos, and 2 adult witnesses.
Legal Reality: A notary affidavit alone does NOT constitute a complete marriage without government Kazi Nikahnama registration.
Legal Protection: Simultaneous affidavit and Kabinnama documentation provides absolute immunity against false abduction (Nari-O-Shishu) charges.

sections.heading: 1. Legal Definition & Reality of Court Marriage in Bangladesh
sections.content: Contrary to common belief, judicial magistrates in Bangladesh do not solemnize marriages directly on the courtroom bench. Instead, court marriage refers to the lawful execution of a sworn Special Affidavit of Marriage affirming mutual free consent, majority, and sound mental health, followed immediately by religious solemnization and official registration with a licensed Marriage Registrar (Kazi).

sections.heading: 2. Essential Documents Required (Checklist)
sections.content:
Both parties must provide the following documentation:

  • Proof of Age: Valid NID cards, Smart Cards, passports, or verifiable online digital birth certificates (English/Bangla 17-digit format).
  • Photographs: 4 recent passport-size photographs of each party.
  • Witness Identifications: Copies of NID cards of at least two adult witnesses of sound mind.
  • Divorce or Death Certificate: If either party was previously married, certified Talaknama or death certificate of previous spouse.

sections.heading: 3. Breakdown of Government Fees, Stamp Duty & Lawyer Charges (2026)
sections.content:
Overall expenditure comprises non-judicial stamp paper, notarization fees, professional legal drafting, and statutory registration fees:

  • Stamp & Notary Public Costs: Approx. BDT 1,500 - 3,000 depending on stamp denominations.
  • Lawyer Drafting & Certification: BDT 2,000 - 5,000 for robust legal protection drafting.
  • Statutory Kazi Fee: BDT 1,250 per BDT 100,000 dower (Denmohar) value up to BDT 500,000 as per government gazette rates.

sections.heading: 4. Why a Notary Affidavit Alone is Incomplete Without Kazi Registration
sections.content: Under Section 5(2) of the Muslim Marriages and Divorces (Registration) Act 1974, failure to register a Muslim marriage is a punishable offence. Relying solely on a notary paper without a registered Nikahnama creates immense legal hurdles during visa processing, passport amendments, inheritance claims, or maintenance disputes.

sections.heading: 5. Legal Defence Against False Police FIRs and Family Harassment
sections.content: When adult couples marry against parental wishes, disgruntled families sometimes lodge fabricated abduction charges under Section 7/8 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain 2000. Having an impeccably drafted affidavit confirming voluntary consent along with official Kabinnama allows the groom to obtain instantaneous Anticipatory Bail (Agam Jamin) from the High Court Division under Section 498 CrPC.

sections.heading: 6. Step-by-Step Procedure at the Chamber
sections.content:
1. Document verification and age verification.
  2. Drafting the Marriage Affidavit on official Non-Judicial Stamp.
  3. Deposition and affirmation before the Notary Public.
  4. Signing the official Marriage Volume (Nikahnama) with the government Marriage Registrar.

faq.question: How long does the entire court marriage process take?
faq.answer: With proper documentation, the affidavit drafting, notarization, and Nikahnama registration are completed within 2 to 3 hours.

faq.question: Is parental presence or permission legally mandatory?
faq.answer: No. Adult citizens (men aged 21+ and women aged 18+) have the constitutional and legal right to marry of their own volition with 2 adult witnesses.
